issue: Historic PRD milestone vs numbered documentation phase
evidence: START-HERE and roadmap vs PRD titles
disposition: Use roadmap IDs for documentation only. Historic milestones remain source metadata.

issue: Stack adopted in historic PRDs vs open baseline ADRs
evidence: P1 §§34–39; P4 technology direction; baseline DEC-001/002
disposition: Retain Go/SQLite/static UI as strong candidate. Keep implementation authorization and stack decisions open.

issue: Auth simulation buttons in v2.0 notes vs removed in v2.1 release
disposition: Use v2.1 as visual authority. Preserve login, MFA, recovery and reset as simulated flows.
Later v1.6 places failure guidance in main column, technical details in context column. Domain activation requires production proof.

issue: Persona codes and switcher visibility vs authorization
disposition: Preserve raw codes. Server evaluates scoped grants and authorization generation.

issue: Billing and payments source-listed vs optional commercial modules
disposition: Account/customer requirements and commercial module approvals tracked independently.
Recovery transport and optional mail hosting get separate release gates.

issue: One topology candidate vs later multi-node placement
disposition: Initial topology decision stays open. Multi-node commitments require a separate feature decision.

issue: Aspirational memory and recovery goals vs validated limits
disposition: Measure idle and peak on supported tuples. Approve targets before using them as release thresholds.
Use prototype for design and static provenance. New production contracts carry proposed and runtime not run status.

issue: Direct PRD route/role proposals vs shared logical contract
disposition: Phase 23 owns conventions. Actual schemas and route aliases require DEC-012.

issue: Hands-off documentation vs protected future engineering
disposition: Continue documentation automatically. Future execution is bound by recorded scope and human release authority.
